title: WIOT from field to dashboard
summary: Field measurements, remote commands and bench verification
steps: Overview

WIOT brings water and soil measurements from the field to a web dashboard. This illustrated walkthrough follows the active S T M thirty-two release, from a sensor reading to a verified operator command.

title: Two routes to the server
steps: Direct MQTT
A sensor node polls its enabled instruments on a shared R S four eighty-five bus. A direct build sends its status and data through Wi-Fi or a SIM eight hundred modem.
LoRa gateway
A LoRa build sends radio frames to the gateway. The gateway reassembles the message and publishes it to the same scoped M Q T T routes.
Server and dashboard
The Python server validates company, region and node scope, stores the reading, and shows it on the dashboard.

title: From sample to stored record
cards: Poll TUF, Supmea, HNDA and Sondas as enabled.
Keep quality flags with each measurement group.
Write completed samples to the SPI flash journal.
Publish on the independent transmission schedule.
steps: Acquire
The sampling deadline starts a polling cycle. The node also reads battery voltage. Supmea consumption uses changes in cumulative volume and trusted clock time.
Validate
A failed sensor group carries zero values and invalid quality. The other groups remain usable, and the node continues reporting.
Commit
When the external archive is enabled, the node commits completed samples to S P I flash. The retention generation lasts twenty-four elapsed hours.
Report
The transmission deadline sends status, normally using the latest committed sample. Keep its acquisition time separate from the server's receipt time.

title: Trace a command to its outcome
cards: Use the correct company, region and node.
MQTT to the gateway or directly to the node.
The addressed node validates the request.
Correlate the application reply by request ID.
steps: Select target
In the dashboard, choose the company, region and node. Send a get status telemetry request and keep the request identifier.
Forward
A direct node receives the broker command. On the LoRa route, the gateway listens to scoped direct commands and regional broadcasts.
Execute
The intended node handles the request and returns its cached measurement snapshot. Radio acknowledgements cover the individual fragments.
Match reply
Match the application reply on the server to the same request identifier. That reply is the evidence of node handling.

title: Wake for work and recover from stalls
cards: Use NORMAL mode to prove the link first.
Gateway wake probe, then UART RX wake on the leaf.
RTC tracks sampling, reports and watchdog service.
The independent watchdog resets a stalled controller.
steps: Commission
Start with normal power mode. Confirm communications before selecting remote idle, wake on radio, or a supported standby profile.
Wake on radio
In wake on radio mode, the normal gateway sends a wake probe. The leaf wakes on its U A R T receive pin and processes the addressed command.
Schedule
The real-time clock tracks sampling and reporting deadlines separately. It also schedules watchdog service during long idle periods.
Recover
If foreground progress stalls, the watchdog can reset the controller. Record watchdog and power reset counters separately.

title: Flash the board you intend to test
cards: Direct Wi-Fi, direct SIM, LoRa leaf or gateway.
Check the board options and export the image.
Connect ST-Link over SWD and verify the write.
Match the serial identity to the board label.
steps: Choose profile
Open the flashing manual and pick a profile. Check the node identity, role, transport, enabled sensors and power mode before compiling.
Verify
Verify the sketch in Arduino and export the image for the selected board.
Program
Use S T Link and the S W D wiring in the manual. Wait for programming and verification to complete.
Check boot
Open the serial log and reset the board. Match the reported role and node identifier to your label before testing the link.

title: Build evidence at the bench
cards: Receive Status and match a command reply.
Test each simulator device, then faults and recovery.
Check RTC, history, wake and reset behavior.
Keep request IDs, timings, logs and measurements.
steps: Prove the link
Start with one node. Check a status and a correlated command reply. For LoRa, add the second leaf after the first path works.
Exercise sensors
Load the four-sensor simulator fixture. Compare values, then mute devices and verify continued reports with invalid quality.
Test storage and power
Synchronize the clock, check stored history, and test the selected sleep and recovery behavior on the board.
Record results
Capture the image, node identity, request identifiers and measured timing and current. The manual gives expected results for each test group.

title: Open the project handover
cards: Six build profiles and twenty bench test groups.
Thirty detailed flows and editable PowerPoint.
Firmware, server, simulator and release checks.
steps: System report
Use the handover index to open the system report, operator manual, editable flowcharts and source entry points. Record hardware acceptance against the deployed boards and test setup.
